findings.failure_path: A first record can now reach the shadow before the second record is serialized. If serialization or a later write raises, write_shadow exits before ftruncate. The packet shows neither the exception cleanup nor a test that observes the denial and empty inode on this path. Successful-event cleanup does not establish either outcome.
findings.smallest_fix: Include the existing finalizer and failure-path assertion if they cover this case. Otherwise, inject a handled failure after the first record is written and assert that PreToolUse denies and the same shadow inode is empty afterward.

findings.failure_path: M24 removes the initial age filter and both under-lock rechecks together. With the initial filter intact, both fresh fixtures are skipped before locking. A regression that drops only the recheck can therefore pass while a file refreshed between the scan and lock acquisition is truncated or deleted.
findings.smallest_fix: Extend the sweep test so an initially stale shadow and legacy temp become fresh between the first age check and lock acquisition. Assert both retain their contents, and verify that removing each corresponding recheck alone fails its assertion.

findings.failure_path: The release record identifies e187f32 as the reviewed commit. The serializer changed afterward, and the bounded packet contains no make test result tied to that changed tree. A regression in a required lane outside the focused bridge tests could therefore be missed at release.
findings.smallest_fix: Include the make test command, candidate identifier, result and skips for the tree containing the incremental writer. If that run is pending, record the full lane as pending.

skipped_clients.reason: claude belongs to the implementer model family

concern_results.conclusion: On success, the incremental writer emits the same ordered JSONL bytes and truncates at the correct byte count, including for an empty event list. The Partial read change documents the existing range-end separator inference.
Serialization now occurs after writing has begun. The packet omits the cleanup path needed to verify that a handled failure on a later record leaves the validated inode empty.
The loop handles positive short writes. A later serialization or write error skips the final length truncate. The resulting verdict and on-disk state depend on the omitted caller and finalizer.
The fresh shadow and legacy temp now have a free run lock. Both are fresh before scanning begins, so M24 can turn red even if the test would pass with either under-lock age recheck removed.

The delta preserves the JSONL format, record order, file name and hook interface. The fixture quoting handles shell-sensitive paths. The plan explicitly excludes machine-local configuration from bridge acceptance.
The writer changes how bytes reach the existing descriptor. It introduces no persistent format migration, so reverting this delta requires no state conversion.
The delta adds no diagnostics. A deterministic failure test can establish the externally visible PreToolUse verdict and shadow state without logging transcript contents.

M24 tests removal of three checks together. Its reported failure cannot establish that either under-lock recheck is independently protected. The revised separator wording accurately distinguishes compared bytes from the inferred byte.

The runtime change keeps writing through the held descriptor. The material unverified boundary is whether a partially written transcript is emptied and PreToolUse fails closed when a later record fails.

The root contract requires a candidate-bound make test result for hook script changes. The supplied evidence names focused checks and a review of e187f32, but supplies no full-lane result for the subsequent executable delta.
